gaps.sentence: ___ surprised me most was his calm.
gaps.hint: 'what' = the thing that; the sentence has no other subject
gaps.explanation: 'What' means 'the thing that' and acts as subject: 'What surprised me most ...' — 'that' cannot introduce this nominal clause.
'What caused the fire' means 'the thing that caused it'; 'that' cannot act as the subject of this nominal clause.

gaps.sentence: I'll never forget the day ___ we first met.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'on which' after time nouns like day, year and moment.

gaps.sentence: That was the year ___ the company nearly went bankrupt.
gaps.hint: time: it happened in that year
gaps.explanation: 'When' is used after 'the year'; 'which' would need 'in which'.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ hand in their essays late will lose marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to the students performing the action; the verb 'will lose' follows later in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: Tell me ___ you said to her.
gaps.explanation: 'What you said' means 'the words that you said'; 'that' cannot head the clause after 'me'.

gaps.sentence: We stayed in a hotel ___ overlooked the harbour.
gaps.explanation: Here the hotel does the action ('overlooked'), so 'which' is needed, not 'where'.

gaps.sentence: This is the worst storm ___ we have had for years.
gaps.hint: after a superlative ('the worst'), use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'That' follows superlatives in defining relative clauses; 'which' is considered poor style there.
